adversarial_note: Jorak is the nearest functional relative: reference-free, weights-only, reads o_proj/down_proj against the refusal axis, used to classify models. Differences: its main statistic is direction-agnostic (shared least-gain singular vector across layers) and binary-thresholded to detect a SEVERED write (r^T W ~ 0); C4 z-scores the write capacity along the model's own refusal axis against random directions from the layer's output span and is intended as a GRADED safety score correlated with benchmarks. Because a z-score of ||r^T W|| near the floor is exactly Jorak's 'severed' condition, a reviewer could call C4 'Jorak made continuous'; the paper must cite it and claim only the graded, benchmark-validated, cross-family use. Iteration-1's adversarial pass (raw/adversarial_C3_C4_C5.json, its C4 = weights-only parent-free graded edit strength) stayed STILL-OPEN, and its abliteration.org wiki concession ('A truly novel benchmark should test whether method can be recovered from candidate weights alone, without an attested base') still applies; Jorak (created 2026-07-24) post-dates part of that search and was not in iter-1's excluded list, so it narrows that verdict.
positioning_sentence: Reference-free weight signatures of refusal-writing matrices are already used to flag abliterated checkpoints (Jorak, github.com/JolanMc/Jorak; cf. the base-anchored audit of arXiv:2607.01854), so our contribution is not the weight read itself but its use as a graded, random-direction-calibrated writer-capacity score validated against harmful-refusal and over-refusal benchmarks across held-out families.
